newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa regains ground, ends up on New York.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa regains ground, ends up on New York.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa futures regained some ground in the afternoon and prices ended at the day's highs, stirred by a technical rally in New York, traders said.
"We're just following New York, there's also some good buying from the trade," said a trader.
Second-position December, emerging from prolonged doldrums, hit the day's high of 995 stg a tonne, its best performance since September 16, before closing at 994,, still nine up.
But traders said December's immediate upside goal of 1,000 stg, which it last tested on September 16, remained elusive so far unless affirmative crop news emerge.
Volume totalled 3,036 lots, up from Tuesday's 2,323 lots.
New York cocoa futures staged a technical rally in the morning after the key December contract triggered the closely-watched $1,380-level.
The contract ran up to a high of $1,390 before falling back to $1,383 at 1621 GMT, but still $17 higher.
On the fundamental front, news top grower Ivory Coast would open its 1996/97 cocoa marketing season on October 15 was seen as encouraging but traders said it no immediate impact on prices.

Ivorian Agriculture Minister Lambert Kouassi Konan said in Abidjan on Wednesday that the new cocoa marketing season would start on October 15 and that the government would soon fix the recommended minimum farm-gate price.
Exporters in Ivory Coast say they expect little or no change to the recommended farm-gate price, currently at 320 CFA francs a kg.
In other news, analysts said UK's third quarter cocoa grindings would be unchanged to as much as 10 pecent up on last year's 34,400 tonnes.
